note: The blueprint's identifier prefixes. `registered` is Appendix A -- Complete Identifier Registry by Prefix, which the document names its allocation authority and which states that an identifier outside it is a defect. The other three lists exist because the document does not obey its own appendix, and a graph that indexed only the appendix would miss 390 real identifiers.

matching.note: A leading guard of (?<![A-Z0-9-]) is REQUIRED when building a regex from these. Without it `\bAI-` matches inside `FAIL-AI-01` and invents an identifier `AI-01` that exists nowhere -- 60 phantoms in one chapter, which made a correct extraction measure as 74%. The same shape read `DEC-ROLE-001` as a `ROLE-001`. Alternation must also be longest-first so `SCHED` cannot claim `SCHEDRUN-001`.

unregisteredButPresent.note: Substantive product content with no Appendix A row -- failure modes, training records, matrices, validation rules, non-goals, alerts, single points of failure, exclusions, AI modes, diagrams, dashboards, delegations, emergency paths. Appendix A calls their absence a defect in the DOCUMENT; dropping real content to make a registry look tidy would be deciding a source question by omission. 388 of these 390 identifiers were captured by extraction agents unprompted, which is a fair sign they read as real to a careful reader too.

illustrative.note: The worked example (a fictional bicycle manufacturer). The blueprint marks it `Illustrative Example` and states it creates no requirement. Left in, the graph's busiest neighbourhood is a worked example and a reader asking what the product must do gets answers about a bike shop that does not exist. The ESC/CHK/TCK/BB group all carry the same instance number 4471, which is what identifies them as one example's paperwork rather than four families.

externalStandards.note: Citations to other people's documents, not identifiers this blueprint allocates. ISA-101, IEC-62264, ISO-TS-9241, ANSI, MIL-STD, ASD-STE100, 21 CFR Part 11, MESA, a Kafka improvement proposal, the EU AI Act, SHA-256, and NIST AI RMF subcategory codes (MS-, MG-, GV-). Counting them as blueprint identifiers would report the graph as missing content it was never meant to hold.
